correctness.rationale: The product law (k,e)(l,f)=(k+(-1)^e l,e+f) proves the full Parikh criterion. For even parameter the quotient types are n residues before seeing b and four parities after; explicit suffixes separate them except the four-state n=2 collapse. For odd parameter there are 2n-1 initial-layer quotients and 2n positive-b quotients, all separately distinguished. The all-parameter argument uses exact Myhill–Nerode equivalence, not finite observations. A standalone independent group-DP and quotient-pair distinguisher passed 4,445 group-count and 11,747 word checks across n=2..30.

value.rationale: Determines the exact deterministic state-complexity invariant for the canonical rotation/reflection positive identity language of every dihedral group, extending the general bounds in Hoffmann 2020. The sharp parity change yields opposite directions of state-complexity change under commutative closure and is explained by the geometry of the quotient predicates (cyclic tails versus saturating thresholds). This structural all-family classification is not an arbitrary finite computation or a routine corollary of the cited regularity theorem.
